text:
Lina M: Heads-up from today's brainstorm 1: we need a trimmed battlecard and SDR cheat for next week's webinar push. Focus: practical rebuttals + routing rules.
Pete W: Got it. Can we keep the battlecard to a single page with 4 quick checks an AE can run in the first minute?
Ravi S: Proposed 4 checks:
- "Do you have firm latency SLOs or just best-effort?"
- "How often do you re-pin models or change model providers?"
- "Where do you run inference today (cloud API / self-host / hybrid)?"
- "What's your peak QPS and budget envelope?"
Tess H: Love the checks. For rebuttals, short and snappy:
- Cloud AI claim: "All-in-one is easiest" -> Reply: "Maybe now. But ease without controls = unpredictable cost and downtime in production."
- Infra vendor claim: "We give you full control" -> Reply: "Control + tooling = outcomes. Show them our rollout + fallback story."
- LLM API claim: "Bigger models => better" -> Reply: "In production, predictability and cost per query often beat raw model size."
Pete W: Include a one-sentence proof point under each rebuttal. Eg: "Customers saw 3x fewer timeouts after adding routing + KV caching." (we'll anonymize).
Lina M: We also need 3 short taglines to test in paid + landing page. Keep distinct from past variants. My suggestions:
A) "Control inference costs. Keep SLAs."
B) "Same serving surface from laptop to VPC."
C) "Automatic fallbacks when models fail."
Ravi S: For inbound routing (ops-bot rules) draft below. Keep tags minimal so SDRs can filter quickly.
```
if text matches any_of(["benchmark","latency","SLA","timeouts"]) -> tag:performance; route:#sales-growth
if text matches any_of(["on-prem","VPC","air-gapped","hsm"]) -> tag:enterprise; route:#sales-enterprise
if text matches any_of(["pricing","cost per token","unit cost"]) -> tag:pricing; route:#revops
if text contains "demo" -> tag:demo; route:#solutions
else -> tag:inbound; route:#sales-queue
```
Tess H: Add a quick SDR 30s script for playbook (super short):
Lina M: "Hi {name}, I'm Lina from Redwood. We help teams make inference predictable across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. Quick Q: do you have latency SLOs or are you optimizing for cost?" -> route based on answer.
Pete W: Perfect. Also include a single chart idea for the benchmark post: normalized cost per 1k requests at 99th pct latency target. Keep axes simple.
Ravi S: I'll create the chart mock and sample assumptions (gpu type, QPS, token per request).
Lina M: Tess, can you produce the one-pager copy and 2-slide AE deck by Thursday? Pete, you own the SDR cheat doc and ops-bot PR. Ravi, chart by Wednesday.
Tess H: On it 680
Pete W: Will open a PR for routing rules and the SD R cheat by Friday EOD.
Ravi S: Chart mock incoming Wednesday.
ops-bot: Reminder: template for routing PR is at https://redwood.app/internal/ops/routing-templates. Use label "marketing-inbound". :robot_face:
Lina M: Final ask: keep language sharp and avoid absolute performance claims. Use comparative language and one anonymized customer line where possible. We'll review in Monday's marketing review.
Tess H: +1
Pete W: +1
Ravi S: +1
Lina M: Thanks team. I'll draft the battlecard layout and drop in the shared drive.
